english: A dog was guarding the rams (sheep). Then a she-wolf arrived and said to him: 'Dog, give me a sheep and I will go away.' He said: 'I do not give her (the sheep) to you. The sheep are not mine; they are the master's.' The she-wolf went away. He who guards does not give a sheep to the wolf.
uncertain: méne: read as GEN 1SG 'mine'; analyzer also offers IMP 'stay!'
wĺ̥kʷōy: masculine 'wolf' (DAT) in the moral while the story's actor is a she-wolf; read as generic
tā́m: fem ACC.SG, taken to refer to h₂ówim (h₂ówis is feminine)
misfit: téh₂es: feminine NOM.PL 'they' referring back to moysṓs (masculine thematic 'rams'); expected masc tóy

english: Son, give water to the guest. Seat the guest at the fire. Do not drive the guest away. He who gives to the guest gives to the gods. When the guest arrives, stand up. Cook for the guest.
uncertain: deywóybʰos: DAT/ABL PL; DAT 'to the gods' fits

english: A wolf saw a dog and said to him: 'Dog, you are full (well-fed). I am thirsty.' The dog said: 'Wolf, follow me; the master feeds me.' 'Are you free?' 'I am not free.' 'Then, dog, I will not follow you.' The free one is thirsty; the full one is not free.
uncertain: tr̥syóh₂/tr̥syéti: lexicon gives only 'to be thirsty' (a 'hungry' wolf might be intended)
sékʷoh₂er: MID PRS 1SG 'I follow' or SBJV 'I shall follow'; also homograph 'say'
h₁léwdʰeros h₁ési?: question marked only by punctuation; speaker presumably the wolf

english: A brother does not kill a brother. A mother nourishes her daughter. A daughter follows her mother. Do not abandon your own father. The brothers died (brothers die); you too will die. Good fame does not perish.
uncertain: mérs: AOR 2SG of 'die' ('you died/die', gnomic) or IMP/AOR of mérst 'forget'; 'die' fits the parallel
misfit: mért: AOR 3SG with plural subject bʰréh₂teres (NOM.PL); expected 3PL

english: The horses said: 'Listen, sheep! Our heart is pained seeing this: man, the master, makes the wool of the sheep into a warm garment for himself, and the sheep have no wool.'
uncertain: whole text: written in Schleicher's 1868 orthography (akwāsas, wawakant, krudʰi, awai, kard agʰnutai...), not the corpus notation; the analyzer recognizes none of it (only 'swas' matched, spuriously). Translated from the known Schleicher fable forms
wiwidwant- swas: split compound 'seeing (us)'; hyphen and space look like a tokenization artifact

english: Son, listen to your own father. Do not strike your brother. Do not tell a lie to your father. A sister follows her brother. Two brothers carry a load. Father and mother nourish the daughter.
uncertain: swóm: reflexive possessive used with 2nd person addressee ('your own')

english: A bird saw a snake creeping toward a mouse. She spoke to him (the mouse): 'Mouse, the snake is creeping toward you. Go away!' He heard her and went away. The snake did not catch him. He who listens to a good word is saved.
uncertain: múHsm̥ sérpontm̥ h₁ógʷʰim: three accusatives with no conjunction; read the mouse as goal of the creeping snake ('saw a snake creeping at a mouse'); could also be 'saw a mouse and a creeping snake'
múHs: form doubles as NOM/VOC; read VOC in the warning

english: Two rams were standing in the field. One was old, the other was young. Then snow came. The young one said: 'I am big. I do not fear the snow.' The old one said: 'I know the snow. My heart trembles.' The young one froze (became cold). The young one is big; the old one knows.
uncertain: stéwdt: 'became cold', possibly implying froze to death

english: The sheep and the horses.
Having heard this, the sheep fled into the field (plain).
uncertain: whole text: mixed older orthography (owis, aǵrom without laryngeals, augmented ebʰuget); only tod and ḱeḱluwōs are recognized by the analyzer
aǵrom: ACC of goal 'into the field'

english: When you see an old man, young one, stand up. Listen to the old man; he knows. Youth goes away. The year makes the father old. The young one grew up. He who works grows strong.
uncertain: h₂yuHn̥téh₂ h₂epó léytt: gnomic aorist 'youth departs'

english: Son, the giver of good things is praised. He who does not give is not praised. The guest belongs to the gods. Death seized (seizes) the old man. The guest sits at the fire. He who is able, let him give.
uncertain: deywṓm gʰóstis h₁ésti: GEN.PL predicate 'the guest is the gods''
h₁épt: aorist, read as gnomic 'death takes the old'

english: Young one, lead the guest to the fire. Feed the guest. Do not kill the guest. He who listens to the word remembers. A famous name does not perish. The young learns from the old. The old man knows.
uncertain: péh₂wr̥: ACC of goal 'to the fire'

english: An old dog caught a she-wolf. She got away. The master was beating the old dog. The dog said to the master: 'I was young, master, and I guarded the sheep. Now I am old. Do not beat me. Remember the work of the old.'
What is it to which the guest and the cattle and the bird go, and which came forth from the earth? It is a spring (well).
uncertain: h₂éwis: NOM 'bird' (also GEN/ABL of 'sheep'); bird fits the list
h₁yód: neuter relative as ACC of goal 'to which'

english: A big fish (catfish) was swimming in the water, and the fish (swam too). The catfish said to the fish: 'Who is master of the water?' The fish became afraid and said to the catfish: 'Catfish, you are master of the water.' The catfish ate a fish. The great one devours the fish.
uncertain: péyskm̥ vs dʰǵʰúHes: two different words for 'fish'
misfit: sn̥h₂wé: 1st person DUAL ('we two swam' / 'we two caught') with plural 3rd-person subject dʰǵʰúHes; expected 3PL

english: A sheep was drinking water at the spring. Then a wolf came and said to her: 'Sheep, you are drinking my water. Who gave you my water?' She said: 'The water is not yours. The spring belongs to the gods.' He seized her. The wolf seeks a sheep and finds a pretext (a word).
uncertain: moysóm: 'ram/sheep' used for the h₂ówis of the story

english: A bird was sitting in a hazel tree. A she-wolf saw her and said to her: 'Come down! Your voice is good (beautiful). Let me hear your voice.' The bird said: 'She-wolf, you are telling a lie. I know you. I will not come down.' The she-wolf went away. He who listens to the word of a she-wolf dies.
What is it in which a fish lives, which a sheep drinks, in which fire perishes? That is water.
uncertain: néḱt: aorist among presents, read as gnomic 'perishes / goes out'

english: The rams (sheep) were trembling. They came to the she-wolf and said to her: 'She-wolf, protect us from the wolves.' She said: 'I will protect you.' Then she ate them. The wolf does not guard sheep; it eats them.
uncertain: h₁ludʰónt: AOR 3PL 'arrived' with ACC of goal (also participle forms)
misfit: tā́s (1st occurrence, 'she ate them'): feminine ACC.PL referring to moysṓs (masculine 'rams'); expected tóms. (The 2nd tā́s, for h₂ówins, is fine since h₂ówis is feminine.)

english: Son, the king guards the sheep from the wolf. The king is the giver of good things. The king's name stands (firm). The king does not kill the guest. Fame follows the king's work. Even the king dies.
uncertain: ḱléwos h₃rēǵés wérǵom sékʷetor: GEN h₃rēǵés can go with either noun: 'fame follows the king's work' or 'the king's fame follows (his) work'

english: Young one, work at dawn. Do your own work. Work nourishes the one who works. He who sits does not eat. He who ploughs the field eats. He who has toiled has grown rich.
uncertain: tóm ... h₁yós: masc ACC antecedent 'him who'
misfit: h₂élete: 2nd person PLURAL verb (PRS/PST/IMP) where the subject is wérǵom (3SG); expected h₂életi

english: The ram (sheep) was speaking to the dog: 'I bear wool. What do you do?' The dog said: 'I do the master's work. I protect him.' The master heard the two of them and said to them: 'The ram's work is great, and the dog's work is great. Each of you do your own work.'
uncertain: tóm h₂léksoh₂: masc ACC 3rd person 'him/that one' (the master? the ram?); if the dog means 'I protect you' (to the ram) one would expect te
misfit: tóybʰos: DAT/ABL PLURAL 'to them' for the pair just named with dual tóh₁; expected a dual form

english: What is it that comes, that goes, that makes the father old, and in which the young one grew up? It is the year.
What is it that warms the earth, that dries the wool, that grows bright at dawn? It is the sun.
uncertain: h₂wést: AOR 'became bright (at dawn)'; homograph PST of 'dwell'

english: Young one, seek imperishable fame. Fame follows work. He who does work, his name is among the famous (is famous). The god hears you well. Do not seek deceit. Remember work.
misfit: ḱlutṓys: INSTRUMENTAL PLURAL 'with/among the famous ones' as predicate of h₁nómn̥ (NOM.SG neuter); expected ḱlutóm 'famous' (cf. ḱlutóm h₁nómn̥ in 239e7c73). Possible but strained as comitative

english: A bird sat down at the spring. Then it saw a fish and said to it: 'Fish, you swim in the water, and I go up to the sky.' The fish said: 'Bird, I do not go up, and you do not swim. The sky is the bird's, the water is the fish's.'
uncertain: dyḗm: ACC of goal 'to the sky'
h₂wéyey / piskéy: DAT of possession 'belongs to'

english: Who is he whom you hear, but have not seen, who drives the snow? It is the wind.
